newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Canadian police to visit Jakarta over Busang scandal.
newsitem.headline: Canadian police to visit Jakarta over Busang scandal.

text.p: A Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) team is expected in Jakarta this week to question people involved in the Busang gold scandal, Indonesian police said on Wednesday.

"Officers from the Royal Canadian Mounted Police are expected to arrive either tomorrow or Friday," said Brigadier-General Ahwil Luthan, secretary of the National Central Bureau which handles investigations requiring Interpol assistance.
"We do not know their schedule yet, but they are likely to interview people involved with the Busang project, including local partners," he told Reuters.

An independent report released on Sunday concluded that the Busang gold site, discovered by Canadian exploration company Bre-X Minerals Ltd, contained no gold worth mining and said data had been falsified on a massive and unprecendented scale.

The RCMP said earlier this week that investigators from its commercial crime unit were studying the report, compiled by Consultant Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd for Bre-X, but it said no formal probe had been launched.
Luthan said his department had begun gathering evidence on Busang, investigating the debacle for commercial crime. The gold find had once been touted as one of the biggest this century.
"We have asked for information from the ministry of mines and energy and it is expected to come through the national police department," he added.
"We are gathering evidence...from the death of the Filipino geologist (Michael de Guzman)...it starts from there," he said.
De Guzman, chief geologist of Bre-X, fell to his death from a helicopter on his way to the Busang gold property in East Kalimantan province.

One week after de Guzman's death in March, Bre-X's Busang partner Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc announced that its test drillings at the property as part of an evaluation or due diligence showed "insignificant" amounts of gold.
Strathcona said in the report that data on the Busang property had been falsified on a scale "without precedent in mining history".
An official at the Philippines embassy in Jakarta said on Wednesday the mission had received an Indonesian police report concluding that de Guzman had committed suicide.

"The report based its conclusion on circumstantial evidence, testimony from the helicopter pilot and co-pilot," the official told Reuters. "The report also said the safety belt and door in the helicopter were in good working order."
Freeport, the Indonesian government and the Nusamba Group linked to President Suharto has pulled out of the Busang project since the Strathcona report was released.
